content.text: Actually, I do not believe that UI assets are always http, but rather the base URL used to serve those assets are the same as the requesting URL.
, the proxy_pass directive is requesting http resources:
The proxy_pass is correct for a termination proxy;  It's accepting TLS requests from the outside world, decrypting (TLS/SSL termination), and proxying the requests to Fedora unencrypted.
The user/browser in the outside world is using https, but gets back html that says:

That's an unencrypted http link.  The baseuri is good except for protocol, which does not match the original request (which was https).  The browser is refusing to load it because it is violating the mixed content rule.  In order for it to work, one or more of the following needs to be true:
HSTS and/or CSP directives instruct the client to ignore stated protocol and always uses https
The link in the html is https instead of http
The link is relative, so the browser uses the same protocol as the initlial request (http)
Agreed. I was just clarify the description of this issue:
Links to UI assets (css, js, etc) are always http
So the proxy's URL-rewriting is rewriting
I'm not opposed to making some provision for customizing the asset base URL, but it seems like a bug in the proxy's URL-rewriting if it doesn't correctly rewrite the protocol when rewriting URLs.

In general, all a reverse proxy does in terms of rewriting occurs in http headers.  The entity bodies are considered opaque and are unmodified (except for stuff like decrypting, transfer encoding, and other transport-related stuff).  This is very lightweight.
The problem is that links within the

fedora produces (in this case, the html for the UI) contain plain links.  Inspecting those documents and modifying them (e.g to re-write URIs) is a specialized task, requiring knowledge of the media types, etc.  Essentially you're piping the response through a specialized grep   I know nginx and apache also have modules that can do that too.  The problem is that this is more heavyweight and resource-intensive than simple proxying.

For something as simple and straightforward as TLS/SSL termination, usually the expense of re-writing entity bodies is not justified.  That's why headers like X-Forwarded-Proto exist:  So that they can give the web apps the information they need in order to create a document that doesn't have to be rewritten.  So it would be a win if Fedora supports that.

Links to UI assets (css, js, etc) are always http, even if the repository is behind an SSL termination proxy, and the X-Forwarded-Proto header indicates https.
Suggestions on on the table include allowing the protocol in hyperlinks to be relative, configurable, or reactive to X-Forwarded-Proto.

comments.body:
Actually, I do not believe that UI assets are always http, but rather the base URL used to serve those assets are the same as the requesting URL.

In the case of https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1208 , the proxy_pass directive is requesting http resources:

> proxy_pass http://c1mckay-sgki99-fedoraerror-8080;

The proxy_pass is correct for a termination proxy;  It's accepting TLS requests from the outside world, decrypting (TLS/SSL termination), and proxying the requests to Fedora unencrypted. 

The user/browser in the outside world is using https, but gets back html that says:

<script type="text/javascript" src="[http://sgki99-fedoraerror.workbench.nationaldataservice.org/fcrepo/rest/fcr:assets/common.js]"></script>

That's an unencrypted http link.  The baseuri is good except for protocol, which does not match the original request (which was https).  The browser is refusing to load it because it is violating the mixed content rule.  In order for it to work, one or more of the following needs to be true:

  • HSTS and/or CSP directives instruct the client to ignore stated protocol and always uses https
  • The link in the html is https instead of http
  • The link is relative, so the browser uses the same protocol as the initlial request (http)

Agreed. I was just clarify the description of this issue:

Links to UI assets (css, js, etc) are always http

So the proxy's URL-rewriting is rewriting http://c1mckay-sgki99-fedoraerror-8080 to http://sgki99-fedoraerror.workbench.nationaldataservice.org instead of https://sgki99-fedoraerror.workbench.nationaldataservice.org?

I'm not opposed to making some provision for customizing the asset base URL, but it seems like a bug in the proxy's URL-rewriting if it doesn't correctly rewrite the protocol when rewriting URLs.

In general, all a reverse proxy does in terms of rewriting occurs in http headers.  The entity bodies are considered opaque and are unmodified (except for stuff like decrypting, transfer encoding, and other transport-related stuff).  This is very lightweight.

The problem is that links within the documents fedora produces (in this case, the html for the UI) contain plain links.  Inspecting those documents and modifying them (e.g to re-write URIs) is a specialized task, requiring knowledge of the media types, etc.  Essentially you're piping the response through a specialized grep   I know nginx and apache also have modules that can do that too.  The problem is that this is more heavyweight and resource-intensive than simple proxying.

For something as simple and straightforward as TLS/SSL termination, usually the expense of re-writing entity bodies is not justified.  That's why headers like X-Forwarded-Proto exist:  So that they can give the web apps the information they need in order to create a document that doesn't have to be rewritten.  So it would be a win if Fedora supports that.

Thanks, Aaron Birkland. Since there are many places in the codebase that rely on the Jersey request context for the uriInfo, it would seem that the ideal option here would be to use the value of the X-Forwarded-Proto header, if it exists, otherwise use the Jersey-injected uriInfo.

Although the getRequestUriBuilder().scheme() approach could help with the /fcr:assets URLs, it is likely insufficient for the variety of other places in the codebase that rely on uriInfo.
I am experimenting with removing the entire $uriBuilder from common-head.vsl along the lines of the submitted PR, if I can get it to work I can make the suggestion on that PR.

Thanks, Jared Whiklo.

That will probably resolve the issue of https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1208 .

Aaron Birkland raises the larger question of potentially using the value of the X-Forwarded-Proto header for in URLs found in the body of HTTP responses.

...but incremental progress is good.

My suggestion is here but boils down to making references from /static which takes them outside the Jersey URI map of /rest. It also moves the common.js and common.css into this /static location because it makes sense that they not be in with the Velocity templates. Lastly moving the common.(js|css) means that the ViewAssets class is not used.

Just an FYI, I have a wrapper solution to support the Forwarded header in fcrepo.  It wraps the UriInfo class and injects it postContruct in FedoraLdp. We have been using the implementation at the UCD library for a couple months now and thought I would make you aware.

 

Repo:

https://github.com/UCDavisLibrary/fcrepo4

Wrapper:

https://github.com/UCDavisLibrary/fcrepo4/blob/fcrepo-4.7.5-headers/fcrepo-http-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/api/FedoraUrlInfoWrapper.java

Inject:

https://github.com/UCDavisLibrary/fcrepo4/blob/fcrepo-4.7.5-headers/fcrepo-http-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/api/FedoraLdp.java#L175
